== Biography ==
'''Ann Jane Glasgow''' was born about 1833 in County Antrim, Ireland. In the 1851 census she was an eighteen-year-old linen weaver in the Glenleslie household of [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]], where she was explicitly recorded as his granddaughter.<ref name="Census1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Glenleslie/21/ 1851 Census of Ireland], Glenleslie household 21, John Glasgow household.</ref>

On 24 November 1869 Ann Jane Glasgow married Patrick Russell. The original register describes her as a thirty-three-year-old spinster of Kildowney and names her father as [[Glasgow-2981|James Glasgow]], weaver. Patrick was a twenty-four-year-old mason of Kildowney, son of John Russell, mason.<ref name="Marriage1869">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Patrick Russell and Ann Jane Glasgow, 24 November 1869, Ballymena registration district; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1869/11434/8200208.pdf original register image].</ref>

The census and marriage concern the same local woman: the ages differ by about three years, but both place her in Dunaghy parish, and James's family was independently recorded at Glenleslie in 1847. Together the records identify James as Ann's father and John as James's father. Ann's mother has not been identified.
A marriage for Anne Glasgow and Russell was registered on 24 November 1869 in the Ballymena district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 24 November 1869, Ballymena district, M/1869/H1/227/1/195.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2981]] is assessed at 93% (proved). Ann Jane’s 1869 marriage explicitly names James Glasgow, weaver, as father; the 1851 Glenleslie granddaughter and James’s 1847 Glenleslie family supply the local identity bridge. The approximately three-year age variation and common father name leave a modest uncertainty about this particular James profile.

Held citation and associated historical narrative address this selected father-child identity; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Find Ann’s baptism or another record naming James with Glenleslie relatives.

No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
